correctness.rationale: The quotient is spanned by 1,x,y,z=xy and the stated table defines an associative four-dimensional model, since all triple products in J vanish. The nilpotent ideal J is the radical and the scalar quotient is k. Over a commutative k-algebra R the unit criterion is exactly that the scalar part be invertible. Writing the remaining factor as 1+ax+by+cz, its last multiplication coordinate is c+c′+ab′+λba′. Subtracting λ(a+a′)(b+b′) and dividing by 1−λ gives the Heisenberg ab′ term and a polynomial inverse. This uses no division by 2. The commutator coefficients generate exactly the minors ideal, with scalar and z coordinates free, proving a scheme identity including s=1. Radical isomorphisms induce scalar congruence of B_λ. Rank separates λ=0; for nonzero λ the cosquare has eigenvalue multiset {λ,λ^−1}, which is unchanged by scalar congruence. Interchanging x and y supplies the converse. Inversion on the nonzero allowed parameters has only −1 fixed in odd characteristic and none in characteristic two; adding the 0 class yields ceil(q/2). Counting the zero matrix and a unique column line for each nonzero rank-one matrix yields q^(2s)((q+1)q^s−q), including 2673 at (q,s)=(3,2). A split-local algebra of dimension ≤3 either has zero radical square or has one radical generator modulo its square and is spanned by 1,x,x², so is commutative. At q=2 there is only one class in this family and no reconstruction counterexample claimed there. The standard-library replay path is `python3 verify.py`; inspection confirms it checks 769,916 multiplicativity and 57 congruence cases over four prime fields, ranks at s=2,3, and small-field pair counts. The script was not executed and does not substitute for functorial proofs.
